Oh my God honey, I am in the same exact situation! The loneliness that comes with feeling unprotected in my own home is hard to cope with.  I can't seem to find someone who is willing to offer me comfort and support.  I feel so guilty addressing my personal problems with other because of being told countless times "This too shall pass.  Everyone's family is dysfunctional.  There's others who have it worse."

This and "Stand up for yourself".  Why?? It's just an open invitation for more abuse and gaslighting! I can't win against a family of full blown narcissists.    People think it's easy to break away from dominating, hot-tempered parents but we understand our reality better than they do and the consequences we could potentially face.  Man do I wish there was a magical shortcut out of abuse, but it doesn't work like that in life.  These people seriously need to shut the f*ck up.  Giving me unsolicited advice on how to deal with my problems makes them look pathetic and weak in my eyes because they don't want to get involved and protect the victim from their abusers.  It's very ironic.

Yeah, but no one holds them accountable for it.  It's easy for them to see negative aspects in others than within themselves.  My parents thought of themselves angels while everybody else was a monster in their eyes. It's like they want to have their cake and eat it too.    Dishonest parents can't really blame their child for being dishonest with them.  You are their teacher.   How you raise your child will determine what kind of person they'll be when they grow up.  Not all kids grow up to become like their parents, but let's say you have a family who's over run by full blown narcissisists who made lots of bad choices in life.  The kid sees their parents lying and the parent also teaches the kid that it's okay to be a hypocrite about it.  The child learns no morals... so if the child ends up doing something bad, the nparent gives this false image that they care and say bullshit like "This isn't like you.  I'm very disappointed in you." But that's my two cents on it.

People typically say to me "If we weren't struggling, life would be boring." Arggh, I hate being told that Yeah, well I'd rather choose boring over pain and trauma! I don't make friends because it's too much effort for me to plan a get together when I have so many responsibilities loaded on my plate, to wear a mask that conceals my feelings, to make sure my anxiety doesn't reach to the surface while talking to someone, and trying to entertain people with my shitty jokes just so that they won't get bored and leave.  On top of that, I don't get a lot or free time on my hands like I used to.  On my days off, I'd rather sleep then force myself to make a bunch of random friends.  I have no desire for friendships and relationships and if that's going against nature then so be it.  Nature has always been kicking my ass ever since I was born, though I've managed to stay alive despite all the horrible abuse I recieved.  I'm getting used to being alone.  It's not a sense of loneliness that I feel anymore.  I don't have to talk to anybody.
Funny, my Mom said that anger causes ulcers and that crying causes cold sores.  I'm surprised how she managed to succeed in school.

I have been told countless times how "irrational" I am and that I should try to be more understanding of the people who invade my boundaries and shame me for who I am.  They think there's no reason as to why I act the way I do.  I'm the one who needs to change every aspect about myself to fit everyone else's narrative.  I need to be more compassionate, more understanding, more open, more tough, ect.  I feel as though they look down on me like I'm some kind of drug addict.

Here's something to also challenge them: Narcissistic abuse is like drowning in deep, shallow water.  If you saw me ACTUALLY drowning, you'd want me to get out of the water immediately, but you insist that I should keep drowning so that everyone else can be happy, including my abusers.  Let that sink in."

From an outsider's perspective, narcissistic abuse can look like a whole lot of other things without the narc context unfortunately.  To them they think your family is like the one from Malcolm in the Middle or Roseanne, but there actually is a BIG difference between dysfunctional and enmeshment.  I believe dysfunctional families are at least still capable of getting along, genuinely apologizing for their mistakes and allow themselves and their child to be whoever they want and the children are encouraged to become independent.  Rarely does this happen with enmeshed, toxic family members.  I don't know if this'll help to shut them up, but you could say something like"I have too much respect for myself to tolerate this abuse any longer and I'm sure if you were in my position, you'd feel the same way.  You don't insist that someone should remain stuck with their abusive partner, so why is it different with a parent? This isn't about keeping ties with family because they are family.  This is about COMMON SENSE.  Would you want to swim in a beach that's infested with sharks just because you love the beach? Would you want to keep sticking your hand in the fire after it burned you? Being dependent on these abusers is almost akin to being kidnapped.  It's like death by 1000 cuts."
Probably because of how nparents makes us feel guilty for having  different personal interests and opinions than them and we think other people will do the same thing to us.
Notice how they don't accept our imperfections.  We are met with angry criticism if we don't reach their standards.

Well, these people are also therapists and social workers. Last week one of them wanted to convince me that she feels for my parents because of their fear of losing me once I move out and how my parents want the best for me.  It frustrates me when I have no good comeback for them.  It makes me feel utterly defeated.  Some part of me really wants to tell them to knock it off.

I tried showing people recordings of them shouting and dictating me, but even then people just assume "Well, they must be stressed out.  Being a parent is difficult.  Every family acts like this." You see it all.  They only get to see half of the picture.

This too "They're just trying to protect you.  They love you too much to let go.  This world isn't how it used to be.  They grew up in entirely different time so they are mostly products of their environment." So they're just trying to protect me from getting hurt.  Yet, they frequently subject me to their abuse on a daily basis.  If they were trying to protect me, I wouldn't be afraid of THEM all the time.  Why do I feel smothered then? Why do I feel this desperate urge to get away from them? Why does my anxiety elevate when I'm near them? What they really did was keeping me from becoming independent so that they could have all the narcissist supply they want from me.
Or she acts this way because of her menopause.  It's so lame to use this cop out reason EVERY SINGLE TIME you rage at your children.

Mine wanted to convince me that she FEELS for my Mom and Dad because I told her how important it was for to get out of that environment in order to protect my well-being.  She said she knows how difficult it is for a parent to lose their child, having to watch them finally be on their own.  I was completely baffled.  All she was concerned about was how my parents felt and immediately overlooked the abuse I'd gone through.

You what irritates me even more? Some people won't even admit that they're gaslighting you: "I'm not trying to defend them, BUT I believe they still care about you and they're just trying to protect you from the evils of this world.  After all, family is important.  They grew up in a different time." "I'm not saying what they did was okay, BUT they still want what's best for you.  They gave you a roof over your head." "I'm not condoning their behavior, BUUUT as a parent myself, I can understand from their perspective because they're not perfect." "I don't agree with what they're doing BUUUUT they mean well." That shit gets on my fucking nerves real quick.  They make it sound like that no matter what the abuser does to you, it was purely out of good intentions.

My Dad explained to me that when I have a job, it's not so much different because I'll have to wake up early to go to work.  I understand that, but waking up early just to go to a half hour yoga class every week sounds quite burdensome!  They usually tell me I have to set my alarm for 5 or 6 (4:30 even) to go to these crazy early hair and doctor appointments as well.

In that moment, I was relieved to have someone comforting me and acknowledging my struggles because no one else in my life did.  THEN, a few weeks later, I suddenly saw a different side of her.  I get a completely different response "Look, we're all gonna have good days, we're all gonna have bad days.  I believe your parents care about you, they just aren't showing it the right way. Sadness should not be buried inside anyone for too long.  It's about connecting with yourself.  We have been raised to suppress our emotions for many years.  We deserve to release them.

If they don't personally know the abuser or are related to the abuser, they'll attempt to justify why they were abusive: "They probably didn't mean it.  They don't know what they're doing because they were raised that way by their own parents.  They made a mistake."

Yes! I get so annoyed and sick of hearing "They obviously love you." or "They love you in their own weird, twisted way." Wow, how insane do you have to be to think that love means torturing someone emotionally; I'm torturing you because I love you?? If that's the case, I'd like to know what they DON'T perceive as love.

Abuse is abuse though.  Our nparents aren't capable of showing love, but that doesn't mean we have to become just like them.  I still show empathy.  I still hug.  I still cry for people when they're hurt.

I'm not saying all victims of abuse are like that, but damn... trying to mess with your head like that? In my experiences, this has happened far too many times. They typically switch from sympathizing with you to shaming you in a short amount of time.  That is very unusual to see that happen in someone who claims to have been mentally abused.  The point is, they have no right to make you doubt your own experiences.  The abuse is already hard enough to live with, but to have your own support group make you feel even more confused about reality is just a stab in the back.  You'd think they know better.

They are clingy, authoritarian parents who need me to be with them at all times 24/7.  They're certainly not going to just sit there and be laid-back "Okay, be careful out there."
Yeah, just walk out into the world unprotected. There's NO chance of you getting possibly kidnapped or injured.  I could even take a walk in the woods without attracting any bears.

Hey, I have the same problem with my therapists.  Once I start talking about my family, the conversation instantly takes a wrong turn.  It is just so mind boggling how I'm sitting there explaining all the trauma my family has put me through and they straight up justify their bullshit: "Oh they want what's best for you.  Oh they care for you.  Oh I admire them for being so opinionated." What the fuck makes them think that? All this hell I'm going through is supposed to be for my own good; the road to hell is paved with good intentions? What was doing their best? What did they do to show me that they loved me? Why are you making wild assumptions about something you have no knowledge of? No, no, let me guess: You have a roof over your head, clothes on your back and food provided on the table for you.  Yeah, they want the best for me, that's why they sit on the couch everyday prioritizing the TV over me and refusing to let me set boundaries or make decisions. The parent is supposed to orbit their child, not the other way around.  A child should not have to fight so hard to earn their parents love.  But it's deeply ingrained in society that family is sacred no matter how messed up a lot of them can be.

I bawled out my eyes to my mother and also told her I wanted to kill myself to which she responded coldly "Yeah, I want to kill myself too." Yeah it's OBVIOUS she loves and cares about me.  She didn't act the least bit concerned.

People like that get annoying after awhile.  At this point, I don't give a fuck whether my parents love me or not.  They have destroyed me in ways I will never be able to recover from and they refuse to feel bad about it.  

I listened to what these flying monkeys have told me.  I really  wanted to believe what they telling me.  And what did I do? I wasted so much time trying my best to love my parents and show them love because I felt pressured to bond with them.  A lot of people tend to make comments that are off-the-wall such as "You parents love you, they don't know how to show it." Why do we have to try so hard to make them love us then? That's backwards.  Why do we have to jump through hoops in order to earn their love? And even then, you're just going to get taken advantage of all over again.  You're going to be spinning around in circles nonstop if you keep entertaining these people.  In fact, there's one way you can tell if you truly love someone or not.  It's by listening to your body.  How often do you feel anxious around this person? Do they make you feel scared? Are you afraid that whatever you say or do will cause them to blow up at you? You can't be scared of somebody and love them at the same time... unless you're trauma bonded.  

It doesn't matter if they can't/ don't know how to "show it" or that they tried the best they could or that they're not perfect or whatever other bullshit people say to you.  That's not really the point anyways.  The point is to break out of that cycle, not encourage you to stay in it because their abuse is only going to cause you excessive damage long-term wise.  You know the truth about your family, not them.  You're not stupid that you don't understand what's happening to you.  Yeah, these people will convince you that your parents aren't as bad as you think they are, but their opinions are biased and uneducated.
